title: Hierarchical A/B Experiment Framework with Adaptive Exposure & Auto-Rollback
creator: Samira Patel
description: Build a robust A/B testing framework for model versions that supports hierarchical experiments (global -> cohort -> variant), adaptive exposure schedules, shadow and canary traffic modes, and automatic rollback based on multi-metric statistical checks and safety sentinels. This ticket captures product requirements, success criteria, integration touchpoints with the Redwood runtime (routing, KV cache awareness), and the ops workflow for incident-safe rollouts. Goal: enable teams to run conservative to aggressive experiments with clear decision rules and minimal manual intervention.
acceptance_criteria: Experiment API supports defining experiments with up to three hierarchical layers: global, cohort, and variant-level overrides.
Adaptive exposure scheduler can ramp or shrink exposure automatically according to user-configured policies (fixed schedule, performance-triggered ramp, or traffic-budgeted adaptive allocation).

Statistical engine runs sequential checks (both frequentist and Bayesian e-value options) and evaluates a configurable set of metrics (latency P95, token cost per request, hallucination rate, correctness metric) with clear pass/fail rules.
Safety sentinels (user-defined thresholds) trigger immediate rollback and notify stakeholders when critical metrics degrade beyond thresholds (e.g., hallucination rate > X, latency > SLA + Y ms).

Shadow traffic mode supported: duplicates of production requests may be sent to candidate models without impacting user-visible responses; metrics from shadow traffic are visible in the console and can feed early-warning alerts.
Integration with Redwood routing layer so experiments can be applied at tenant, region, or route granularity and use consistent KV cache warming to avoid cold-start artifacts.
Experiment audit logs, decision history, and ability to manually override auto-rollback preserved for compliance and debugging.

End-to-end demo: run a hierarchical experiment that ramps a quantized variant from 1% to 30% using adaptive exposure and show automated rollback when hallucination metric crosses sentinel within 24 hours.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: API + metadata model: define experiment schema (layers, metrics, sentinels, rollout policies, data retention).
Phase 2: Scheduler + routing integration: implement adaptive exposure controller in the control plane and wire to runtime routing API (canary/shadow/batch modes).
Phase 3: Statistical engine: add sequential testing modules (optional frequentist group sequential with alpha-spending, and Bayesian e-value-based checks) and tie to metrics pipeline.
Phase 4: Safety sentinels & auto-rollback: configure immediate rollback paths and notification hooks (PagerDuty/Slack/Console).
Phase 5: Observability + audit: dashboards per-experiment showing allocation, metric trajectories, decisions, and raw samples; store audit trail in immutable log for 90+ days.
Phase 6: Docs & demo: run internal pilot with two product teams and produce runbook + training.
Phase 7: Launch: gated launch with opt-in beta customers, collect feedback, iterate on thresholds and UI affordances.
design_decisions: Use hierarchical experiment model so defaults can be specified globally and overridden at cohort/route level to reduce configuration duplication.

Expose two statistical modes: a conservative frequentist sequential option (alpha spending, pre-specified look schedule) and a continuous Bayesian e-value approach for rapid feedback and decision-making.
Adaptive allocation should be dampened to avoid over-committing traffic to ephemeral signals; use a smoothing window (configurable) and a hard cap per-interval.
Safety sentinels are declarative per-experiment metric thresholds with immediate rollback semantics; non-critical regressions create slow-rollback policies instead of instant revert.
Shadow traffic must not write side-effects to downstream systems; provide a sandboxed execution path with same model runtime but I/O gating for unsafe ops.
testing_plan: Unit tests for experiment schema validation and policy parsing.
Integration tests simulating traffic ramps with mocked runtime to verify allocation and rollback flows (canary, shadow, and A/B splits).
Statistical engine validation using historical datasets: verify Type I/II behavior for frequentist mode and calibration for Bayesian mode using synthetic drift scenarios.
Chaos test: inject transient latency spikes and verify that KV cache warming and rollout smoothing prevent noisy auto-rollbacks.
Pilot with internal teams: instrument 3 small experiments including a neutral control to validate baseline noise and false-trigger rate.
observability_and_alerts: Per-experiment dashboard: allocation timeline, cohort summaries, per-metric control vs. treatment trajectories with confidence bands.
Alert types: info (trend), warning (metric approaching sentinel), critical (sentinel breached -> auto-rollback).
Notification sinks: Console banner, Slack channel + thread, PagerDuty incident for critical safety sentinel breaches.
Drilldown: sample-level traces and request IDs for all candidate responses (shadow traffic included) to enable quick RCA without replaying production traffic.
Cost tracking: token-level cost delta per-experiment to evaluate economic tradeoffs when promoting heavier-weight models.
